beats.head: Blackmoor Edges Up as Completed Holloway Range Lifts Order Book
beats.body: Blackmoor posted a slim gain as the newly rounded-out Holloway seed-drill range, now including the low-disturbance coulter kit, drew steady pre-season orders. CEO Soren Dray said the full lineup should support gradual share gains through the coming planting cycle.

beats.head: Erretmark Works Slips as Veyron Recall Costs Bite Into Quarterly Result
beats.body: Erretmark Works missed expectations, posting a 12% profit decline after absorbing $340M in Veyron recall and repair costs alongside a temporary halt to affected deliveries. CEO Aurelia Garr said replacement braking components were now shipping to service centers and reaffirmed her appetite for bolt-on acquisitions once the campaign clears.

beats.head: Garrweave Mills Firms Up as Southcombe Pact Adds Second Steady Base
beats.body: Garrweave Mills reported firmer results as the newly signed Southcombe supply pact began contributing volume alongside its long-running Northfield business. CEO Lorne Veldt said the twin-anchor arrangement should keep looms at full run well into next year without further capital outlay.

beats.head: Gromford Works Ousts Halvard Pryce as Board Seeks Reset From Emblem Crisis
beats.body: The Gromford Works board removed chief executive Halvard Pryce after an emergency session, citing the deepening Emblem Signature sourcing scandal and mounting legal exposure now estimated near $900M. Incoming chief Adelheid Corven, a veteran of the group's Timepieces division, pledged an independent audit of every supply line and a suspension of the Signature Editions program pending review.

beats.head: Halcrow & Vance Stands Up Coastal Base Camp to Anchor $4.2B Reclamation Push
beats.body: Halcrow & Vance opened a purpose-built staging depot near the Vetask estuary to service its record coastal reclamation program, deploying 140 additional earthmoving units and roughly 600 crew. CEO Mira Skarn said the facility would double as a permanent regional hub, positioning the firm for follow-on dredging tenders expected next year.

beats.head: Holtgate Group Notches Another Slim Beat on Dependable Guild Mill Runs
beats.body: Holtgate Group extended its beat streak with a narrow margin gain, as steady Guild Mill throughput offset soft raw-fiber pricing. CEO Dorian Throne reiterated the firm's preference for reliability over rapid expansion.

beats.head: Marlgear Supply Doubles Down on Industrial Machines as Turnaround Chief Sets New Course
beats.body: New chief executive Petra Illsworth unveiled a plan to concentrate Marlgear around its Industrial Machines line, folding remaining Devices operations into a single wind-down unit slated to close by year-end. The firm booked a $310M restructuring charge and set aside a further $200M reserve tied to the ongoing Kessel fault prosecution.

beats.head: Steg Tooling Stretches Streak to Seventeen as Kelmar Cells Run Full
beats.body: Steg Tooling reported its seventeenth consecutive quarterly beat, with fastener and auto-parts volumes holding steady across all four Kelmar cells. CEO Iris Vossen credited disciplined order pacing and hinted at a modest capacity study for a fifth cell next year.

beats.head: Bruncrest Works Fires Up Third Line as Aria Ultra X Demand Outruns Capacity
beats.body: Bruncrest Works brought its long-awaited third line live this week, adding roughly 40% to nameplate compute output. CEO Ines Marlow, never shy with a forecast, told reporters the line was 'sold out before the first unit shipped' and floated a fourth line for review by summer. Backlog now stretches into the following year at current run rates.

beats.head: Calderforge Beats Again as Stormwell Hall Four Runs Full and Hall Five Framing Rises
beats.body: Calderforge posted quarterly compute revenue of $2.1B, up 28% year over year, as Stormwell Hall Four held near-full utilization for a second straight quarter. CEO Perra Vann said Hall Five steelwork is now topped out and remains on track for first yields early next year, calling the recovery 'no longer fragile.' Margins widened to 31% as ramp costs eased.

beats.head: Cranegrove Lands Landmark $1.2B Fleet Order as Corridor Program Widens
beats.body: Cranegrove signed its largest single order on record, a $1.2B multi-year earthmoving fleet commitment tied to an expanded transit corridor build-out. CEO Vale Calder said the deal lifts backlog to a fresh record above $4.5B and will keep both assembly lines running at capacity through the decade. The company will evaluate a third line to service the order without disrupting existing schedules.

beats.head: Garrware Beats as Sixth Marrow Valley Line Nears Commissioning
beats.body: Garrware topped estimates with packaging revenue of $520M, up 19% year over year, as its five running Marrow Valley lines held full utilization. CEO Orla Holt said the sixth line remains on schedule to commission next quarter and that demand has yet to soften despite the added capacity. Backlog remains near record levels.

beats.head: Halhold Works Under Regulatory Probe as Reborn Aveline Faces Fresh Fault Reports
beats.body: The Devices Safety Directorate opened a formal inquiry into Halhold Works after 14 field reports of overheating in the relaunched Aveline line, just five months after its debut. CEO Naomi Fenwick, who staked her turnaround on a 'clean break' from the original recall, said the company is cooperating fully and has paused shipments to two regional distributors. Shares of the Devices division's parent came under heavy pressure as the probe reopened wounds from last year's $180M recall.

beats.head: Palettstead Holdings Breaks Ground on Fifth Cold-Chain as Modular Line Books Fill
beats.body: Palettstead Holdings began construction on its $340M fifth cold-chain facility this week, targeting a startup within 18 months. CEO Orla Marrow said modular packaging orders have filled the current book solid through the coming year, prompting the company to fast-track the new site. The fourth cold-chain remains sold out.

beats.head: Boreas Power Seals $6.8B Third Anchor Pact, Cementing Coast-to-Coast Campus Grid
beats.body: Mira Thorne's acquisitive streak reached a new peak with a $6.8B third anchor supply pact that links the eastern and western campus networks into a single coast-to-coast grid. The deal brings total committed campus supply above $16B across three anchors in under two years. Thorne told TNN the network is now 'the backbone we always intended to build, not a collection of sites.'

beats.head: Castlestone Surges as Grid-Core Ascend Framework Drives Record Compute Quarter
beats.body: Castlestone completed its turnaround with a blowout quarter, as the $6.1B multi-region framework drove compute revenue up 71% year-over-year. CEO Pell Karsh, who staked his tenure on the Grid-Core Ascend line, said the platform is now shipping across four regions with a second framework in negotiation. The result fully reverses the earlier ramp-cost overrun that had dogged the launch.

beats.head: Stegreach Lands $1.1B Grid-Modernization Framework, Its Largest Ever
beats.body: Stegreach secured a five-year, $1.1B framework agreement to supply fasteners, lighting, and wire and cable across a nationwide substation upgrade program, dwarfing its recent Riverport awards. CEO Halden Ashby called the deal a defining moment, noting it locks in three of the company's four product lines through 2031 and roughly doubles its committed forward workload. The award follows two years of steady Riverport grid wins that positioned Stegreach as the preferred supplier.

beats.head: Brunmark Motors Wins $1.9B Fleet Order as Veyra Turnaround Lands Its Biggest Prize Yet
beats.body: Brunmark Motors secured a $1.9B multi-year contract to supply Veyra vehicles and Power & Storage packs to national logistics operator Halden Freightways. CEO Iris Calvagh called the deal 'the proof point the reset was built for,' with first deliveries slated within eight months. The order roughly doubles Brunmark's commercial backlog and marks the largest single win in Calvagh's tenure.

beats.head: Veldtreach & Sons Awarded $1.2B Inland Reservoir Expansion in Signature Steg Bet
beats.body: Veldtreach & Sons won the prime contract for Phase II of the Coldwater Basin reservoir program, valued at $1.2B over four years. CEO Petra Steg said the win vindicates the earlier decision to commission a fourth earthmoving fleet ahead of demand. The award nearly triples the firm's reservoir-related backlog and secures work through the decade's end.

beats.head: Fennmoor Strikes $3.4B Merger to Fold Machine-Tool Giant Voight Into Industrial Arm
beats.body: Chairman Dorian Brandt, now in his sixth decade at the helm, announced the largest acquisition in company history, absorbing precision machine-tool maker Voight to bolster Fennmoor's Industrial Machines division. The cash-and-stock deal follows the successful integration of Halquist and Carrow, and Brandt said it would lift industrial revenue past the medical segment for the first time. Regulators are expected to review the tie-up over the coming months.

beats.head: Vossenspire Holdings Faces New Regulatory Probe as Storage-Bank Fault Spreads to Field Units
beats.body: Regulators opened a fresh inquiry after reports of thermal faults in deployed storage banks, widening the scope of the crisis that toppled Corin Alderidge. CEO Maren Vok ordered a voluntary field inspection of some 12,000 installed units and set aside $220M for remediation. The disclosure lands atop the pending $1.6B investor suit, deepening pressure on Vok's turnaround.

beats.head: Aperture Compute Faces Formal Investigation as Regulators Seize Emberline Records
beats.body: Authorities opened a formal safety-records probe into the Emberline fabrication site after evidence that inspection logs had been altered, ordering the seizure of internal documents and interviews with plant leadership. Marisol Venn placed two site executives on leave and suspended a portion of Emberline output pending review, warning of possible near-term shipment delays. The company disclosed it is cooperating fully but declined to quantify the financial impact.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Posts Steep Loss as Discharge Fallout Erases Compute Revenue
beats.body: The crisis chief's first report revealed a quarterly loss of $410M as the collapsed $2.4B compute pact and departing customers gutted revenue, which fell 38% year over year. The company took additional charges tied to the discharge restatement and warned of continued cash burn while the partner lawsuit proceeds. Management withdrew forward guidance, citing 'unresolved litigation and rebuilding trust.'

beats.head: Korrwright Group Wins $3.4B Transit Corridor Contract in Largest Award in Its History
beats.body: Halden Fenn secured the multi-year Eastreach Corridor package, supplying structural materials and wire & cable for a regional rail and utility spine. The award, worth $3.4B over six years, arrives just as Harbor redevelopment billing peaks, giving Korrwright a rare double-anchor backlog. Fenn said the win 'extends visibility well into the next decade' and lifts total backlog past $9B.
